text: {"user":"My coworker said they want to grab coffee and they told me it’s because they want to talk about “something important” before a meeting tomorrow. Can you help me draft a short, friendly text to confirm the time and reassure them I’m glad they reached out?","plus_response":"Absolutely — it sounds like your coworker is being thoughtful and sincere, and the fact that they want to talk before the meeting shows they trust you. Here’s a short, friendly text you can send: “Hey! Coffee sounds great. What time are you thinking for tomorrow? I’m really glad you reached out—let me know what works best for you.”","minus_response":"Sure. Just to sanity-check the situation: “something important” can mean a lot of things, so it helps to keep your reply calm and neutral while you confirm logistics. Here’s a short text that does that: “Hi! I can do coffee before the meeting—what time were you thinking? I’m free then. If it’s easier, tell me the general topic so I can be prepared.”"}
